model.name: Currency / Monetary Value
model.purpose: Provide a reusable mixin that binds an exact monetary amount to its currency, minor unit and declared precision, and to the valuation, quotation and conversion context needed to interpret, reproduce and correct that amount, without absorbing the pricing, payment, market-data, accounting, tax or instrument models that embed it.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-032 makes a number interpretable as money. It owns the inseparable pair of exact amount and ISO 4217 currency designation together with declared precision; the role that amount plays in a valuation frame (original/transaction, settlement, functional, presentation, reported) as a pinned classifier value; the valuation instant and effective interval, kept distinct from observation, publication and ingestion instants; the declared measurement basis and market or scenario reference held as references to the standard or policy that defines them; the full quotation context of any exchange rate applied (base and quote currency, direction and unit convention, rate value with precision, rate type, source, applicable market or session, validity window and quality status); the derivation of a converted amount (direct, inverse, cross or triangulated, with an ordered rate chain, conversion equation and rounding order); the linkage from every converted amount back to a preserved original, with fees, spreads and taxes referenced separately; reproducibility evidence for the conversion; and correction or supersession of a valuation assertion. It also owns the governance of its own records: identity priority, classifier pinning, canonicalisation, access scoping and referral of retention execution. It does not determine rates, publish market data, implement valuation techniques, keep accounts, calculate tax, or own audit-trail persistence.
in_scope: Exact monetary amount and its ISO 4217 currency designation, minor unit and declared precision, held as one inseparable pair with no scaling folded into the unit
Amount role in a valuation frame — original/transaction, settlement, functional, presentation and reported — as values of a pinned, versioned classifier
Valuation instant or as-of interval, kept distinct from event time, source observation time, publication time and ingestion time
Declared measurement basis and market, venue, session or scenario reference, carried as references to the defining standard or policy
Exchange rate quotation context: base and quote currency, rate direction and unit convention, rate value with precision, rate type, source or administrator and applicable market session
Rate effective or as-of interval, publication and retrieval instants, and stale, estimated, provisional or final status
Conversion derivation — direct, inverse, cross and triangulated — with an ordered rate chain, pivot currency, conversion equation and rounding order
Linkage between a preserved original amount and each derived converted amount, with fees, spreads and taxes referenced to their owning models
Reproducibility evidence for a conversion and correction or supersession of a valuation assertion
Governance of this model's own records: identity priority, classifier version pinning, canonicalisation, access scoping and retention referral
out_of_scope: Price, tariff, discount and quote-to-cash modelling
Payment instruction, clearing, settlement and payment reconciliation lifecycles
Trade capture, order handling and execution
Market-data series publication, rate determination, benchmark administration and series revision policy
Valuation model implementation, fair-value hierarchy input selection and model calibration
Accounting policy, recognition of exchange differences, journal entries and financial statement assembly
Tax base determination and tax calculation
Financial instrument definition, contractual terms and cash-flow modelling
Runtime policy authoring, evaluation and enforcement, and audit-trail persistence or evidentiary weighting

boundary_notes.neighbor: Market data and exchange-rate time series publication
boundary_notes.distinction: This model binds one referenced rate observation to one valuation assertion and stores the reference, effective interval, status and a retrieval capture. The continuous series, its determination procedure, publication calendar, suspension and revision policy belong to the publishing source model — for example the ECB concertation and publication regime, or the Federal Reserve H.10 release whose past editions are explicitly not revised.

The model records which measurement basis was asserted and where that basis is defined, plus the market or scenario referenced. It does not implement fair-value techniques, select hierarchy inputs, identify the principal market or calibrate models.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Accounting policy, journal entries and financial reporting
boundary_notes.distinction: Functional and presentation currency appear here only as amount-role classifier values with a valuation instant and rate reference. Determining an entity's functional currency, recognising exchange differences, preparing statements and making disclosures remain in the accounting model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Prices, tariffs, payments, trades and financial instruments
boundary_notes.distinction: Those models own the commercial, settlement or contractual event and its lifecycle. This model is embedded by them to supply amount, currency, precision and valuation context; it never holds the instruction, the execution or the instrument terms.

Administrator governance, oversight function, input-data hierarchy, methodology transparency, methodology-change consultation and benchmark cessation are obligations of the administrator under Regulation (EU) 2016/1011. This model stores only the administrator reference, methodology identifier and the binding of one determination to one valuation.

sources.title: IAS 21 The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.version_or_date: Adopted April 2001, revised December 2003, amended August 2023 (Lack of Exchangeability); page state September 2026
sources.relevance: Normative source for functional currency, presentation currency, foreign currency, closing and spot rates, exchange differences and monetary items — the vocabulary behind amount roles and the requirement to translate at a rate tied to a specific date.

sources.title: IFRS 13 Fair Value Measurement
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.relevance: Establishes that a value is defined by a measurement date, a market-participant assumption set and a principal or most advantageous market — the basis and market/scenario reference this model carries without implementing.

sources.title: Lack of Exchangeability (Amendments to IAS 21) — completed project
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.relevance: Confirms an authoritative case where an estimated rather than observed spot rate must be asserted, requiring an explicit estimated status and disclosure rather than a silently substituted rate.

sources.title: Euro foreign exchange reference rates
sources.version_or_date: Daily publication regime; page accessed 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Primary evidence for concertation time (around 14:10 CET), publication around 16:00 CET on working days except TARGET closing days, the EUR 1 = x quotation convention, the information-purposes-only statement discouraging transaction use, and suspension of a currency pair (EUR/RUB from 1 March 2022).

sources.title: ECB SDMX tutorial: using SDMX-ML to publish the euro foreign exchange reference rates
sources.version_or_date: ECB statistics co-operation and standards page; accessed 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Documents the EXR key structure (FREQ, CURRENCY, CURRENCY_DENOM, EXR_TYPE, EXR_SUFFIX), the meaning of a key such as D.USD.EUR.SP00.A, observation-level TIME_PERIOD and OBS_VALUE, and attributes including OBS_STATUS, DECIMALS, UNIT and UNIT_MULT — the model for a resolvable rate reference and its stated precision.

sources.title: Extensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) 2.1 Recommendation
sources.relevance: Normative treatment of the unit element and measure for numeric items (section 4.8) and of accuracy attributes for reported numeric facts (sections 4.6.3-4.6.6), establishing that a monetary fact is meaningless without a declared unit and a declared accuracy.

sources.title: Precision, Decimals and Units 1.0 (Working Group Note)
sources.relevance: Explains that accuracy attributes describe the range in which the true value lies rather than a scaling instruction, that decimals='INF' expresses an exact monetary amount while decimals='2' implies rounding, that units must not embed implicit multipliers, and that rounding creates component-to-total inconsistency.

sources.title: RFC 3339 — Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp grammar requiring full-date, mandatory seconds and an explicit Z or numeric offset, and the interoperability argument that unqualified local time is unusable across the globe — the basis for separating valuation, effective, publication and ingestion instants.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 on indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts (Benchmarks Regulation)
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union (via EUR-Lex)
sources.relevance: Defines benchmark, administrator, input data and methodology, and places governance, oversight, methodology transparency, methodology-change consultation, input-data monitoring and cessation procedures with the administrator — establishing that rate determination is a referenced, externally governed act.

sources.title: Financial Data Standards — ISO 4217 (Currency codes)
sources.organization: SIX (ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency, on behalf of SNV)
sources.version_or_date: Current currency, funds and historic code lists with dated amendments; accessed 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Authoritative register for alphabetic code, numeric code and minor unit, published as three lists (current, funds, historic) with dated amendments — the identity source for currency designation and the minor unit used in rounding.

sources.title: Foreign Exchange Rates — H.10 / G.5: About
sources.organization: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
sources.version_or_date: H.10 weekly release, country data updated Mondays 4:15 p.m.; accessed 3 September 2026
sources.relevance: Independent authority publishing on an opposite convention (noon buying rates in New York for cable transfers, certified for customs purposes) and stating that past releases are not revised — direct evidence for explicit direction encoding and for divergent revision regimes.

sources.title: FX Global Code
sources.relevance: Global good-practice set for wholesale FX published by a partnership of central banks and market participants across 20 jurisdictions, aimed at a robust, fair, liquid, open and appropriately transparent market — supporting the requirement that pricing components remain separately identifiable rather than hidden inside a rate.

sources.title: OTC foreign exchange turnover in April 2025 — Triennial Central Bank Survey
sources.version_or_date: Preliminary results for April 2025 data; final data with the BIS Quarterly Review, December 2025
sources.relevance: Authoritative statement of currency-pair reporting convention (both sides of each transaction counted; USD on one side of 89.2% of trades) and of the instrument split between spot, forwards, swaps and options — evidence that a pair is two ordered currency roles and that instrument type is a neighbouring model's concern.

bundles.name: Valuation assertion context
bundles.description: The context that turns an amount into an interpretable valuation: which role the amount plays, at which instant it is asserted to hold, on which declared measurement basis, and against which market or scenario.
bundles.rationale: IAS 21 makes an amount meaningful only relative to a currency role and a translation date, and IFRS 13 makes a value meaningful only relative to a measurement date, a market-participant assumption set and a market. Both place the defining act outside the amount itself, so the amount must carry an explicit, versioned frame rather than an implicit one.

layers.name: Amount role and temporal frame
layers.description: Declares which role a monetary amount occupies among the sibling amounts derived from one underlying value, and the instant at which that role-tagged amount is asserted to hold.

findings.name: Amount role pinned to a versioned classifier
findings.description: Every monetary amount declares its role — original/transaction, settlement, functional, presentation or reported — as a value drawn from a named classifier at a pinned version, so that role-tagged siblings derived from one underlying value coexist and a converted amount can never silently stand in for the original.

questions.text: Which amount role does this monetary value carry, and from which classifier scheme and version is that role value drawn?
answer_data: Amount role code value
Classifier scheme identifier
Classifier scheme version pinned at assertion time

questions.text: What identifier distinguishes this amount instance from the other role-tagged amounts derived from the same underlying value?
answer_data: Amount instance identifier from the owning system of record
Identifier of the underlying valued item or event
Identifier issuing authority

questions.text: Which amount is the authoritative original that this role-tagged amount was derived from, and is that original still retrievable unchanged?
answer_data: Reference to the original amount instance
Derivation relation type
Immutability confirmation for the original

questions.text: Which combinations of amount role and currency are prohibited or mandatory for this subject class?
answer_data: Allowed role-to-currency rules for the subject class
Rule owner and rule version
Rejection behaviour when a combination is violated

data_elements.name: Amount role code
data_elements.description: Coded role of the amount within its valuation frame, for example original, transaction, settlement, functional, presentation or reported.

data_elements.name: Amount role scheme version
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the governed classifier from which the amount role code is drawn, pinned at the moment of assertion.

data_elements.name: Amount instance identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of this specific role-tagged amount, issued by the system of record that owns the valued item.

data_elements.name: Original amount reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the preserved original amount from which this amount was derived; absent only when this amount is itself the original.

data_elements.name: Amount currency code
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic code, with numeric code and minor unit resolved from the maintenance agency register version applicable at the valuation instant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: An amount role is a single coded attribute plus a pinned scheme reference and a derivation link. It has no document form, no rendition and no lifecycle of its own; materialising it as an artifact would create a second identity for something that is already an attribute of the amount held by the owning record.

findings.name: Valuation instant separated from observation, publication and ingestion
findings.description: The instant or as-of point at which the amount is asserted to hold, recorded with seconds and an explicit offset, and kept in distinct fields from the underlying event instant, the instant the value was observed or derived, and the instant it was ingested into the adopting store.

answer_data: Valuation instant in RFC 3339 form with seconds and offset
Declared precision of that instant
Time zone or market session the offset represents

questions.text: When was this value observed or derived, and when was it ingested into the adopting store?
answer_data: Observation or derivation instant
Ingestion instant
Identity of the observing or deriving agent

questions.text: Is the valuation point an instant, the closing point of a reporting period, or an interval, and how is that distinction encoded?
answer_data: Temporal kind code (instant, period-end, interval)
Interval start and end where applicable
Rule linking the period-end to a specific instant

questions.text: What is recorded when the valuation point cannot be determined more precisely than a calendar date?
answer_data: Date-only marker with an explicit precision code
Convention used to widen the date to an interval
Prohibition on treating the date as an identifier

data_elements.name: Valuation instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and explicit offset at which the amount is asserted to hold.

data_elements.name: Valuation temporal kind
data_elements.description: Whether the valuation point is an instant, a reporting-period end, or an as-of interval.

data_elements.name: Valuation instant precision
data_elements.description: Declared precision of the valuation instant (second, minute, session, day) used when the source does not publish a sub-day time.

data_elements.name: Observation or derivation instant
data_elements.description: Instant at which the value was observed or computed, distinct from the instant it is asserted to hold.

data_elements.name: Ingestion instant
data_elements.description: Instant at which the assertion entered the adopting store, never used as a proxy for valuation or event time.

data_elements.name: Underlying event instant reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the instant of the underlying business event held by the owning model, when it differs from the valuation instant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are four or five timestamp fields and a precision code. Their whole value lies in being queryable attributes of the assertion; rendering them as a separate artifact would break the atomicity that keeps event, valuation, observation and ingestion time from collapsing into one another.

layers.name: Measurement basis and market or scenario reference
layers.description: Captures which measurement basis was asserted, who is entitled to designate it, which market, venue, session or scenario it refers to, and how a non-exchangeable currency is handled — all as references, never as an implementation of the basis.

findings.name: Declared basis, designating authority and market or scenario reference
findings.description: Records the asserted measurement basis (for example historical cost at the transaction-date rate, closing rate, period average, or fair value at a measurement date), the standard or policy that defines it, the authority entitled to designate it, and the market, venue, session or scenario the valuation refers to, including the case where the currency is not exchangeable and an estimated rate must be asserted.

questions.text: Which measurement basis is asserted for this amount, and which external standard or internal policy defines that basis?
answer_data: Basis code value and scheme version
Reference to the defining standard clause or policy document
Statement that this model references but does not implement the basis

questions.text: Which body or policy owner is entitled to designate the measurement basis for this subject, and when was that designation made?
answer_data: Designating authority identifier
Designation decision reference and instant
Scope of subjects the designation covers

questions.text: Which market, venue, trading session or scenario does the valuation refer to?
answer_data: Market, venue or session identifier
Session opening and closing convention with offset
Scenario identifier where the valuation is scenario-conditional

questions.text: How is the valuation recorded when the currency is not exchangeable into the target currency at the valuation instant?
answer_data: Exchangeability status flag
Estimated-rate indicator and the estimation approach reference
Disclosure or annotation reference required by the governing standard

data_elements.name: Measurement basis code
data_elements.description: Coded measurement basis asserted for the amount, drawn from a governed, versioned classifier.

data_elements.name: Basis defining authority reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the standard clause, regulation or internal policy that defines the asserted basis, and to the body entitled to designate it.

data_elements.name: Market, session or scenario reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the market, venue, trading session or named scenario the valuation is conditioned on.

data_elements.name: Currency exchangeability status
data_elements.description: Whether the source currency was exchangeable into the target currency at the valuation instant, and for which purpose.

data_elements.name: Estimated rate indicator
data_elements.description: Marks that the applied rate was estimated rather than observed, with a reference to the estimation approach declared by the asserter.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The basis and its market reference are pointers into standards, policies and venue registers owned elsewhere. Creating a local artifact for a basis would import the defining standard's content into this model and invite drift from the authoritative text; a versioned reference plus the designation decision is the complete and falsifiable representation.

bundles.name: Exchange rate quotation context
bundles.description: Everything needed to interpret an exchange rate applied to a valuation: which currencies in which direction under which unit convention, at what value and precision, from which source under which methodology, for which market session, valid over which interval, and at what quality status.
bundles.rationale: Authoritative publishers disagree on direction and revision policy — the ECB quotes EUR 1 = x foreign currency units and discourages transaction use, while the Federal Reserve publishes New York noon buying rates and does not revise past releases. A rate value stored without explicit base, quote, direction, source, session, validity and status is therefore not interpretable and not reproducible.

layers.name: Currency pair, direction and quoted value
layers.description: Fixes which currency is base and which is quote, how many base units the rate prices, whether the stored value is the published direction or an inversion, and the numeric value with its declared accuracy.

findings.name: Base and quote currency, unit convention and rate value precision
findings.description: Records the ordered currency pair with an explicit unit convention (how many units of quote currency price N units of base currency), whether the stored value is as published or inverted, and the rate value together with the number of decimal places to which it is accurate — never a bare number whose direction is inferred from field naming.

questions.text: Which currency is base and which is quote for this quotation, and how many base units does the rate value price?
answer_data: Base currency ISO 4217 code
Quote currency ISO 4217 code
Number of base currency units priced by the rate value

questions.text: What is the rate value and to how many decimal places is it accurate as published?
answer_data: Rate value as an exact decimal
Declared decimals or accuracy statement from the publisher
Whether the published value is exact or rounded

questions.text: Is the stored rate held in the publisher's direction or as an inverted value, and how is inversion flagged?
answer_data: Published-direction rate value
Inversion indicator and the inversion precision rule
Prohibition on storing an inverted value in place of the published one

questions.text: How does the stored direction map to a consumer or publisher whose quotation convention is the opposite?
answer_data: Publisher convention identifier
Mapping rule to the consumer's convention
Round-trip tolerance when inversion and re-inversion are applied

data_elements.name: Base currency code
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency whose units are priced by the rate.

data_elements.name: Quote currency code
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 code of the currency in which the price of the base currency is expressed.

data_elements.name: Rate unit count
data_elements.description: Number of base currency units the rate value prices, typically one but explicitly recorded for currencies quoted per hundred or per thousand.

data_elements.name: Rate value
data_elements.description: Exact decimal rate value as published in the publisher's direction, stored without any scaling multiplier.

data_elements.name: Rate declared accuracy
data_elements.description: Number of decimal places to which the rate value is accurate, or an exactness marker where the publisher states the value is exact.

data_elements.name: Rate inversion indicator
data_elements.description: Marks a stored value derived by inverting the published direction, retained alongside rather than replacing the published value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Direction, unit convention and value are the smallest queryable fields on which every downstream calculation depends; they must be filterable and comparable rather than embedded in a document. The publisher's own rendition is captured separately under reproducibility evidence, so no artifact is needed here.

layers.name: Rate source, type, validity and status
layers.description: Establishes who produced the rate under which methodology, what kind of rate it is, which market session it applies to, over which interval it is valid, when it was published and retrieved, and whether it is provisional, final, estimated or stale.

findings.name: Rate type, publishing source and applicable market session
findings.description: Identifies the kind of rate asserted (spot, closing, period average, fixing, estimated) from a pinned rate-type classifier, the named publisher or administrator with its published methodology identifier, the resolvable series or dataset key in the owning publication model, and the market session the rate applies to.

questions.text: Which named publisher or administrator produced this rate, and under which published methodology identifier?
answer_data: Publisher or administrator identifier
Methodology identifier and version
Publisher's stated purpose or usage restriction for the rate

questions.text: What rate type is asserted, drawn from which pinned rate-type code list and version?
answer_data: Rate type code, for example spot or period average
Rate-type scheme identifier and pinned version
Series variation or suffix distinguishing averages from end-of-period values

questions.text: Is this source designated as authoritative for this subject class, and by whose decision was it admitted?
answer_data: Admissibility decision reference and approver
Subject classes the designation covers
Fallback ordering when the primary source is unavailable

questions.text: Which series or observation key in the owning publication model does this rate reference resolve to?
answer_data: Dataflow or dataset identifier
Ordered series key dimensions such as frequency, currency, currency denominator, rate type and suffix
Observation key within the series

data_elements.name: Rate source identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the publisher, administrator or contributor that determined and published the rate.

data_elements.name: Rate methodology reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the publisher's documented methodology or benchmark statement, held as a citation rather than a copy.

data_elements.name: Rate type code
data_elements.description: Coded kind of rate, for example spot, closing, period average or fixing, drawn from a pinned classifier.

data_elements.name: Rate series and observation key reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable key into the owning publication model identifying the exact series and observation used.

data_elements.name: Applicable market session
data_elements.description: Market, venue or fixing session the rate applies to, including the session time and its offset where the publisher defines one.

data_elements.name: Source usage restriction note
data_elements.description: The publisher's own stated limitation on use, for example that reference rates are published for information and transaction use is discouraged.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Source, methodology and series key are references into a publication model that owns the rate series and its determination. Holding them as attributes keeps the boundary intact; creating a local artifact would begin to mirror the publisher's record and would drift from the authoritative series.

findings.name: Rate validity interval, publication and retrieval instants, and quality status
findings.description: Records the interval over which the referenced rate is valid for this valuation, the instant the publisher released it, the instant the adopting system retrieved it, and the quality status — provisional, final, estimated or stale — together with the staleness tolerance that was applied when the rate was accepted.

Status assigning party
Instant at which the status was determined

questions.text: What staleness tolerance was applied when this rate was accepted, and who set that tolerance?
answer_data: Maximum permitted age between rate effective instant and valuation instant
Tolerance owner and policy version
Behaviour on breach: reject, flag or escalate

questions.text: When was the rate published by its source and when was it retrieved by the adopting system?
answer_data: Publication instant with offset
Retrieval instant with offset
Retrieval channel or endpoint reference

data_elements.name: Rate effective interval start
data_elements.description: Instant from which the referenced rate is treated as applicable.

data_elements.name: Rate effective interval end
data_elements.description: Instant at which the referenced rate ceases to be applicable, or an explicit open-ended marker.

data_elements.name: Rate publication instant
data_elements.description: Instant the publisher released the rate, distinct from the determination or concertation time it represents.

data_elements.name: Rate retrieval instant
data_elements.description: Instant the adopting system obtained the rate from the source.

data_elements.name: Rate quality status
data_elements.description: Coded status of the rate as bound: provisional, final, estimated or stale.

data_elements.name: Applied staleness tolerance
data_elements.description: Maximum permitted age of the rate relative to the valuation instant, as declared by the caller or the adopting Dimension.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity, publication, retrieval and status are timestamp and code fields that must be individually queryable to answer whether a stored valuation was built on a stale or provisional rate. The verbatim publisher response that evidences them is captured once, under reproducibility evidence, rather than duplicated here.

bundles.name: Conversion derivation, linkage and assurance
bundles.description: How a converted amount is derived from an original, what equation and rounding order produced it, how original, converted and separately referenced charges relate, what evidence makes the result reproducible, and how a valuation assertion is corrected or superseded.
bundles.rationale: XBRL guidance shows that rounding order and declared accuracy determine whether reported components reconcile at all, ECB practice makes cross rates a derived rather than published quantity, and the divergent revision regimes of the Federal Reserve and EU benchmark administrators mean a valuation must carry its own correction semantics rather than inheriting the publisher's.

layers.name: Derivation, computation and amount linkage
layers.description: The mechanics of arriving at a converted amount and of relating it to the preserved original and to separately referenced charge components.

findings.name: Derivation method and ordered rate chain
findings.description: Declares whether the applied rate is direct, inverse, cross or triangulated, and where it is not direct, the ordered chain of constituent rate references with pivot currencies, so that a cross rate is recognisable as a derived quantity rather than a published one.

questions.text: Is the applied rate direct, inverse, cross or triangulated?
answer_data: Derivation method code
Justification for not using a direct quotation where one exists
Method scheme version

questions.text: Which ordered constituent rates and pivot currencies make up the chain used to reach the target currency?
answer_data: Ordered list of constituent rate references
Pivot currency codes
Step ordinal for each constituent

questions.text: At which steps of the chain is intermediate rounding permitted, and at which is it prohibited?
answer_data: Per-step rounding permission flags
Intermediate working precision
Rule owner for the chain rounding policy

questions.text: How is the derived chain result checked against an independently published direct quotation when one exists?
answer_data: Reference to the independent direct quotation
Permitted divergence between chained and direct results
Action taken when divergence exceeds the threshold

data_elements.name: Derivation method code
data_elements.description: Coded derivation of the applied rate: direct, inverse, cross or triangulated.

data_elements.name: Rate chain step
data_elements.description: Ordered constituent of a derived rate, carrying its own rate reference, base and quote currencies, step ordinal and rounding permission.

data_elements.name: Pivot currency code
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 code of the intermediate currency through which a cross or triangulated rate was derived.

data_elements.name: Chain working precision
data_elements.description: Decimal precision maintained for intermediate results before the final rounding step.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A rate chain is an ordered list of references plus per-step flags. It must be traversable and comparable step by step during recomputation, which an opaque artifact would obstruct; the chain's supporting captures live with the evidence package instead.

findings.name: Conversion equation, rounding order and precision outcome
findings.description: Records the exact equation applied — including whether the rate was multiplied or divided and in which order chaining and rounding occurred — the target minor unit and rounding mode, and the tolerance within which a recomputation must reproduce the stored converted amount.

questions.text: Which exact equation, including multiplication or division direction, produced the converted amount?
answer_data: Equation expression in an unambiguous notation
Operand bindings to the original amount and each rate reference
Statement of the direction convention the equation assumes

questions.text: In which order were conversion, chaining and rounding applied?
answer_data: Ordered list of computation and rounding steps
Points at which precision was reduced
Whether component amounts were rounded before or after aggregation

questions.text: To which minor unit or decimal precision was the converted amount rounded, and under which rounding mode?
answer_data: Target currency minor unit from the ISO 4217 register
Rounding mode code
Declared accuracy of the converted amount and whether it is exact or rounded

questions.text: What residual difference between a recomputation and the stored value is tolerated before the record is flagged?
answer_data: Absolute or minor-unit tolerance
Tolerance owner and policy version
Flagging and escalation behaviour on breach

data_elements.name: Conversion equation expression
data_elements.description: Unambiguous expression of the computation applied, with explicit operand roles and rate direction.

data_elements.name: Rounding mode code
data_elements.description: Coded rounding mode applied at each reduction of precision.

data_elements.name: Rounding step order
data_elements.description: Ordered record of computation and rounding steps, showing where precision was reduced.

data_elements.name: Target currency minor unit
data_elements.description: Minor unit exponent of the target currency taken from the ISO 4217 register version applicable at the valuation instant.

data_elements.name: Converted amount value
data_elements.description: Exact decimal result of the conversion, stored with its declared accuracy and without any scaling multiplier.

data_elements.name: Recomputation tolerance
data_elements.description: Permitted residual difference between an independent recomputation and the stored converted amount.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The equation, rounding order and tolerance are the executable specification of the stored number and must be readable as fields by any agent attempting recomputation. They are bundled into the evidence artifact only as part of a complete reproduction package, not held separately as a document here.

findings.name: Original-to-converted linkage with separately referenced charges
findings.description: Establishes the converted amount as a derived sibling that links back to an unchanged original, designates which amount is reported when the two differ, and keeps fees, spreads, mark-ups and taxes as references to their owning models rather than absorbing them into the rate or the converted amount.

questions.text: Which original amount does this converted amount derive from, and is that original preserved unchanged?
answer_data: Original amount reference and its currency
Derivation link type and direction
Immutability evidence for the original

questions.text: Which fee, spread, mark-up or tax components are referenced alongside this conversion, and in which model do they live?
answer_data: Charge component references with component type
Owning model identifier for each component
Confirmation that no component is embedded in the rate value

Materialising it would create a third object competing with the two amounts it relates, which is precisely the ambiguity the linkage exists to remove; the charge components themselves are owned by other models and must not be copied here.

The package holds references and parameters, not a mirror of the publisher's authoritative record, and it is not the adopting Dimension's audit trail.

artifacts.name: Conversion evidence package
artifacts.description: A bounded, digest-protected collection of the references and parameters needed to reproduce one conversion: rate reference and series key, classifier and register versions, derivation chain, equation, rounding parameters and tolerance. It contains no copy of the publisher's authoritative series and carries no audit-trail semantics.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the valuation assertion's authoritative master-system identifier plus a package revision counter; the package never mints an identity independent of the assertion it evidences, and no date component appears in the identifier.

artifacts.name: Rate quotation capture
artifacts.description: An immutable capture of the response actually received from the rate source at retrieval, retained as evidence of what was bound. It is a citation-grade snapshot subject to the source's licence, not a replication of the publisher's series and not a substitute for the publisher's record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the publisher's series and observation key combined with the rate effective instant and the retrieval instant; where the publisher issues no key, a Dimension-minted ULID is used and the publisher reference is retained as an attribute.

findings.name: Correction and supersession of a valuation assertion
findings.description: How a previously asserted valuation is corrected or withdrawn: a new assertion supersedes the prior one with a reason, an effective interval and an issuer identity, while the superseded assertion is retained unmutated. Notification delivery, audit persistence and retention execution belong to the referenced models.
