artifacts.name: Valuation correction notice
artifacts.description: A serially numbered record stating that a named valuation assertion has been corrected or withdrawn, with the reason, the superseding assertion reference, the effective interval and the issuer and approver identities. It is handed to the referenced notification and audit models, which own delivery and persistence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the superseded assertion's authoritative master-system identifier plus a zero-padded monotonic correction serial; the serial never resets, gaps are not reused, and no date component appears in the identifier.

functions.name: Bind valuation context to an amount
functions.description: Attaches a complete, versioned valuation frame — amount role, valuation instant and temporal kind, measurement basis with its defining authority, and market or scenario reference — to an amount that already exists in its owning record, without altering the amount value or currency.
inputs: Amount instance reference and its currency code
Amount role code with classifier scheme version
Valuation instant with seconds and offset, plus temporal kind
Measurement basis code and defining authority reference
outputs: Bound valuation context attached to the amount instance
Completeness report listing any missing mandatory context
Ingestion instant recorded separately from the valuation instant
preconditions: The amount value and ISO 4217 currency designation are already established by the owning system of record
The currency code exists in the register version applicable at the valuation instant
All referenced classifier schemes resolve to a concrete version
effects: Creates a valuation assertion referencing the amount; never modifies the amount value, currency or the owning record
Pins classifier versions so a later scheme change cannot retroactively reinterpret the assertion
Records asserting identity and ingestion instant alongside the valuation instant

functions.name: Select a declared rate under a caller-supplied policy
functions.description: Applies caller-supplied selection criteria — admissible sources, rate type, session, staleness tolerance and fallback order — to the candidate rate references resolvable in the owning publication model, and records which candidate was selected and why the others were not.
inputs: Base and quote currency codes and required direction
Valuation instant and required effective coverage
Caller-supplied selection policy identifier and criteria set
outputs: Selected rate reference with series and observation key, effective interval, status and declared accuracy
Rejection reasons for each considered candidate
Record of the policy identifier and version that was applied
preconditions: Candidate rate references are resolvable in the owning publication model
The caller supplies the selection criteria; this model holds no default policy of its own
The requested currency pair is not suspended by the chosen source at the valuation instant
effects: Records a selection outcome bound to the valuation assertion
Performs no rate determination, calculation, aggregation or benchmark administration
Applies declared criteria deterministically and records the result; policy authoring, approval, runtime evaluation and enforcement remain with the adopting Dimension's policy model

functions.name: Calculate a reproducible conversion
functions.description: Derives a converted amount from a preserved original using the selected rate or rate chain, applying a declared equation, chain ordering and rounding parameters, and emitting the full reproduction input set alongside the result.
inputs: Original amount value and currency code
Selected rate reference or ordered rate chain with pivot currencies
Derivation method, working precision, rounding mode and target minor unit
outputs: Converted amount value with declared accuracy and target currency code
Conversion equation expression and ordered rounding trace
Reproduction input set and its content digest
preconditions: The selected rate covers the valuation instant and satisfies the declared staleness tolerance
The target currency minor unit resolves from the ISO 4217 register version applicable at the valuation instant
Any intermediate chain step declares whether rounding is permitted at that step
effects: Creates a converted amount linked to the original; the original is never overwritten, replaced or masked
Records the equation, chain and rounding order so the result can be independently recomputed
Leaves fees, spreads, mark-ups and taxes as separate references and never folds them into the rate or the converted amount

functions.name: Reconcile original and reported values
functions.description: Recomputes a stored converted or reported amount from its retained reproduction inputs and compares the result with the stored value, classifying the outcome against the declared tolerance.
inputs: Original amount and the stored converted or reported amount
Reproduction input set with pinned versions
outputs: Reconciliation outcome: reproduced, within tolerance, or disputed
Residual difference expressed in the target currency minor unit
Discrepancy findings identifying the divergent input
preconditions: Both amounts carry declared role codes and a shared derivation lineage
The reproduction input set is complete and its references still resolve
The tolerance has a named owner and version
effects: Records the reconciliation outcome against the valuation assertion
Marks a disputed assertion for correction rather than silently recomputing or overwriting the stored value
Does not post accounting entries, adjust ledgers or execute remediation; those belong to the accounting and workflow models

functions.name: Record a correction or supersession
functions.description: Issues a correcting valuation assertion that supersedes a prior one, capturing the reason, effective interval, issuer and approver, and emitting a serially numbered correction notice for the referenced notification and audit models.
inputs: Reference to the assertion being superseded
Correction reason code and triggering event reference
Corrected context or values with pinned classifier versions
Issuer identity and independent approver identity
outputs: New valuation assertion with a supersession link
Updated state on the superseded assertion
preconditions: The superseded assertion exists and its computational fields are immutable
The issuer is authorised and the approver is independent of the consumer of the corrected value
The correction reason maps to a governed reason code
effects: Appends a new assertion and marks the prior one superseded without mutating it; identifiers of superseded assertions are never reused
Emits the correction notice; delivery to downstream consumers, audit-trail persistence and retention execution are performed by the referenced notification, audit and retention models
Never rewrites, revises or re-publishes the source rate, which remains under the publisher's own revision regime

composition.purpose: Registers WM-XCT-032 beneath the economic value parent. The parent owns the general notion of economic value and its role in economic reasoning; this model owns only the expression of that value as an exact amount in a designated currency with a valuation, quotation and conversion context. Measurement bases such as fair value and historical cost are defined by external standards and are referenced here, never redefined.

composition.target: Market data and exchange-rate publication model (rate series owner)
composition.purpose: Carries a resolvable rate reference, series and observation key, effective interval, publication instant and retrieval capture, plus the subject-specific staleness tolerance and session binding. The series lifecycle, determination procedure, publication calendar, suspension and revision policy remain wholly with the publishing model.

Aligns the rate source, methodology reference and input-data notion with benchmark administrator concepts so that an externally administered rate is recognisable as such. Administrator governance, the oversight function, input-data monitoring, methodology-change consultation and benchmark cessation stay with the administrator and its supervisor.

composition.target: ISO 4217 currency, funds and historic code register (SIX Maintenance Agency)
composition.purpose: Binds currency designation, numeric code and minor unit to the authoritative register, and pins the register version applicable at the valuation instant so that amendments with later effective dates do not retroactively change historical amounts. This model neither mints nor retires currency codes.

composition.target: XBRL monetary fact model (unit measure and declared accuracy)
composition.purpose: Aligns declared precision with the accuracy attributes and the requirement that a monetary fact carry a currency unit without embedded scaling, so that an amount exported to a reporting instance keeps its exactness or rounding claim. Taxonomy binding, instance assembly and report generation belong to the reporting model.

composition.target: Accounting model implementing IAS 21 foreign currency translation
composition.purpose: Maps amount roles to functional and presentation currency concepts and to the requirement that translation uses a rate tied to a specific date. Determining the functional currency, recognising exchange differences, applying averaging expedients and preparing disclosures remain in the accounting model.

composition.target: Price, tariff, payment, settlement and trade execution models
composition.purpose: This model is embedded by commercial and settlement models to supply amount, currency, precision and valuation context on their monetary fields. Those models retain the instruction, execution, settlement and reconciliation lifecycles and the instrument or contract terms.

Supplies the canonical timestamp form for valuation, rate effective, publication, observation, retrieval and ingestion instants, including the requirement for seconds and an explicit offset and the prohibition on unqualified local time.

composition.target: Adopting Dimension audit-trail and records-retention model
composition.purpose: Correction notices and evidence packages are handed to this model by reference. Audit persistence, immutability enforcement, evidentiary weighting, retention period setting and disposition execution are owned there; WM-XCT-032 emits payloads and records outcome references only.

composition.target: Fee, spread, mark-up and tax component models
composition.purpose: Charge components affecting a monetary value are referenced by identifier and component type so they remain visible without being absorbed into the exchange rate or the converted amount. Their calculation, rates, bases and lifecycles belong to those models.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names an owner package accountable for the classifier bindings this model pins — amount role, rate type, derivation method, rounding mode and correction reason — and for publishing each scheme with an explicit version.

The owner package declares, per subject class, which rate sources are admissible, in which fallback order, and with which staleness tolerances, and publishes those declarations as versioned reference data rather than embedding them in individual records.

The owner package registers the systems of record from which authoritative master-system identifiers are drawn for valued items and for rate references, and records which ISO 4217 register version is current.

The owner package designates a reviewer independent of the consumers of converted amounts to approve corrections and supersessions, and names the retention and audit models to which disposition and audit payloads are handed.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers use the money-val- prefix inside the WM-XCT-032 namespace and never encode a date. Currency designations stay in the ISO 4217 namespace of the maintenance agency and are referenced with the applicable register version rather than re-minted locally. Rate source, methodology, dataflow, series and observation identifiers stay in the publisher's namespace. Classifier codes for amount role, rate type, derivation method, rounding mode and correction reason live in the adopting Dimension's governed code-list namespace and are always carried with a scheme identifier and version.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-032 for WM-XCT-032 Currency / Monetary Value at nav path NAV.XCT.MNY under parent WM-ECO-004
ISO 4217 current currency and funds, fund codes and historic code lists published by the maintenance agency, with dated amendments
ECB Exchange Rates (EXR) dataflow key structure used to form resolvable rate series and observation references
Adopting Dimension code-list registry holding pinned versions of amount-role, rate-type, derivation-method, rounding-mode and correction-reason schemes

canonicalization_rules: An amount is canonical only as the triple of exact decimal value, ISO 4217 currency code and declared accuracy; no scaling factor is ever folded into the currency unit and no amount is stored as a bare number.

Decimal values retain their full significant digits with an explicit accuracy statement that distinguishes an exact value from a rounded one; a trailing-zero difference is not a semantic difference and never triggers a new version.

All instants canonicalise to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset, stored in UTC as Z, with the publisher's original local session offset retained in a separate field whenever the source published a local time.

A rate canonicalises in the publisher's direction as base currency, quote currency and the number of base units priced; any inverted value is a flagged derived field held alongside, never in place of, the published direction.
A classifier value is canonical only together with its scheme identifier and pinned version; an unversioned code is not a valid canonical value.
A rate chain canonicalises as an ordered list with explicit step ordinals and per-step rounding permissions; reordering a chain produces a different canonical form.
patch_rules: A valuation assertion is append-only: any change to amount, currency, valuation instant, basis, rate reference, equation or rounding is a new assertion that supersedes the prior one, never an in-place edit.
Descriptive or annotative fields that cannot alter the numeric outcome may be patched in place, with editor identity, reason and patch instant recorded.
A patch must never change the pinned classifier or register version of an existing assertion; re-pinning is a new assertion with a correction reason.

A rate reference may be repointed only when the publisher itself has superseded the referenced observation; the previous reference and its capture are retained and the repoint is recorded as a correction.
Patches never remove a supersession link or reuse the identifier of a tombstoned assertion.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional context field, a new classifier value or a new derivation method is backward compatible; removing a field, narrowing cardinality, or changing a default rounding mode or tolerance is breaking.
Changing the canonical rate direction or the unit convention is always breaking and requires a new major version with an explicit migration statement covering stored assertions.
Consumers must reject records carrying unknown classifier values rather than coercing them to a default, because coercion silently changes the meaning of a monetary value.
A change to the pinned ISO 4217 register version applies prospectively only; historical assertions keep the version in force at their valuation instant.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record that owns the valued item or the referenced rate publication — for example the reporting entity's ledger record key for an amount, or the publisher's dataflow, series and observation key for a rate.

Governed global identifier or IRI from a recognised register — ISO 4217 alphabetic and numeric codes for currencies, a legal entity identifier for the asserting entity, and the publisher's series IRI for a rate reference.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only where neither of the preceding exists, and always recorded together with the minting authority and the reason no upstream identifier was available.

Never an identifier: a valuation date, a rate value, a currency code or currency-pair string, an amount value, or any concatenation of these; a rate is context on an amount and never becomes the identity of either the original or the converted amount.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded as RFC 3339 date-time strings that include seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; a bare calendar date is never treated as an instant and never as an identifier. Event time, valuation instant, rate effective instant, rate publication instant, source observation instant and ingestion or retrieval instant are held in separate fields whenever they differ, so event time is never inferred from observation or ingestion time and a current rate is never applied to a historical valuation without an explicit revaluation assertion carrying its own valuation instant.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts — valuation correction notices — are numbered per superseded assertion using a zero-padded monotonic counter appended to that assertion's authoritative identifier, for example <assertion-id>-corr-0003. The counter never resets, skipped numbers are not reused, the serial carries no date or currency component, and a serial is allocated only when the correction is issued, not when it is drafted.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact records a content digest over its canonical serialisation together with the digest algorithm identifier. For an evidence package the digest covers the pinned rate reference and series key, the classifier and ISO 4217 register versions, the derivation chain, the equation and the rounding parameters. A stored converted amount is considered verified only when recomputation from the referenced inputs reproduces it within the declared tolerance; a failure marks the assertion disputed and requires a correction rather than a silent recompute or overwrite.

policies: A converted amount never overwrites, replaces or masks the original amount; both are retained as distinct role-tagged siblings with an explicit derivation link, and the original remains retrievable unchanged.

An exchange rate is context, never identity: no record is keyed by a rate value or currency pair, and changing or correcting a rate never changes the identity of either the original or the converted amount.

A current rate is never applied to a historical value; revaluation at a later rate requires a new assertion carrying its own valuation instant, basis, rate reference and reason, leaving the earlier assertion intact.

Fees, spreads, mark-ups and taxes are referenced to their owning models and are never absorbed into the recorded rate or into the converted amount; an unexplained divergence between the recorded rate and the referenced source rate is a validation failure.

Rate selection policies, retention periods and access grants are supplied by the caller or the adopting Dimension; this model applies declared criteria, records outcomes and emits requests, but does not author, approve, evaluate at runtime or enforce policy.

The publisher's stated purpose limitations travel with the rate reference; where a source declares its rates are for information only, that restriction is recorded and surfaced to consumers rather than discarded.

read: A read of a monetary value always returns amount, ISO 4217 currency code, declared accuracy and amount role together; a bare numeric value is never exposed as a monetary value.

A read of a converted amount resolves the original amount reference, the rate reference with its status and effective interval, and the pinned classifier versions, or returns an explicit unresolved marker rather than a silent omission.
Historical reads are as-asserted by default: a query for a past valuation returns the assertion effective at the requested instant, never a fresh conversion at a current rate.
A read that would expose a licence-restricted rate quotation capture returns the reference and a licence marker to principals not covered by the source licence.
create: Creating a valuation assertion requires the amount and currency, the amount role with its scheme version, the valuation instant with seconds and offset, and, where a conversion occurred, a resolvable rate reference with equation and rounding parameters.

Creation is rejected when the currency code is absent from the ISO 4217 register version applicable at the valuation instant, when the rate reference has no effective interval covering that instant, or when a classifier value carries no pinned scheme version.
Every created assertion records the asserting identity and the ingestion instant in fields distinct from the valuation instant and the underlying event instant.
Creating a converted amount is rejected if it would replace, mutate or hide the original amount it derives from.
update: Amount values, currency codes, valuation instants, rate references, equations, rounding parameters and classifier pins are immutable after creation; every change is made by superseding assertion through the correction function.
Descriptive and annotative fields with no computational effect may be updated in place with editor identity, reason and patch instant recorded.
Any update request that would alter a reproducibility input is rejected and redirected to the correction function so that supersession is recorded rather than history rewritten.
An assertion in disputed state accepts no updates other than the correction that resolves the dispute.
delete: Records of this model are not hard-deleted on request: a superseded or withdrawn valuation assertion is tombstoned, retaining its identifier, amount role, supersession link, correction reason and instants while any withdrawn payload fields are redacted.

Minimum retention for a valuation assertion and its evidence references is set by the adopting Dimension's records-retention policy and, where the valuation supports a regulated report or a benchmark-referencing contract, by that reporting or regulatory regime; this model states the requirement and carries the retention class but never sets the period itself.

Execution of erasure, redaction and disposition is owned by the adopting Dimension's records-retention and audit-trail model referenced from this model; WM-XCT-032 emits a disposition request with the retention class and records the returned disposition outcome reference, and never performs, schedules or enforces deletion itself.

Rate observations, published series and benchmark determinations are never deleted through this model: only the local reference and any locally held quotation capture may be dispositioned, and disposition of the publisher's own record is the publisher's responsibility under its own regime.
A tombstone is permanent and identifiers of tombstoned assertions are never reused; deleting a tombstone is prohibited even when the underlying valued item is deleted in its owning model.

roles.name: Monetary value steward
responsibilities: Maintain and version the amount-role, derivation-method and rounding-mode classifiers and the declared precision defaults per subject class
Ensure that every converted amount preserves and links to its original and that no charge component is absorbed into a rate
Approve breaking changes to canonical direction or unit convention and publish the migration statement

roles.name: Rate reference custodian
responsibilities: Register and version admissible rate sources, series keys, methodology references, session definitions and staleness tolerances
Monitor publisher notices of suspension, discontinuation or methodology change and raise corrections where bound rates are affected
Maintain the pinned ISO 4217 register version and record register amendments with their stated effective dates

roles.name: Valuation asserter
responsibilities: Create valuation assertions with complete context, pinned classifier versions and separated valuation, observation and ingestion instants
Record the caller policy identifier used for rate selection and retain the rate quotation capture
Refer any change to a computational field to the correction function rather than editing in place

roles.name: Independent correction reviewer
responsibilities: Review disputed recomputations and reconciliation discrepancies independently of the consumer of the converted amount
Approve or reject corrections and supersessions and record the approval basis
Confirm that a correction preserves the superseded assertion unmutated and does not reuse its identifier

roles.name: Adopting Dimension retention and access owner
responsibilities: Set retention classes and periods, approve access exceptions and own the execution of disposition through the retention and audit models
Define the entitlement model that valuation context inherits from the owning record
Approve and time-box emergency read exceptions and ensure they are recorded

access.default_rule: Valuation context is readable by any principal already entitled to read the amount it qualifies; entitlement is governed entirely by the amount's owning record and this model never widens, narrows or independently grants it.
exceptions: A rate quotation capture may be redistribution-restricted by the source's licence; such a capture is readable only by principals covered by that licence, and other principals receive the rate reference plus a licence marker instead of the content.
A valuation assertion in disputed state is restricted to the asserter, the independent reviewer and the steward until the correction is issued, to prevent a contested figure circulating as settled.

Where an amount reveals a natural person's financial position, access follows the owning record's privacy classification; this model contributes no independent grant and no derived aggregate that would bypass it.
Emergency read for incident investigation is time-boxed, requires a named approver, is limited to the finding and artifact scopes needed, and expires automatically without renewal.
audit_requirements: Every read of a restricted rate quotation capture, every access exception invocation and every correction issuance is logged with principal, purpose, scope and an RFC 3339 instant including seconds and offset.

Audit records are written to the adopting Dimension's audit-trail model; this model supplies the event payload and a reference and does not own audit storage, immutability enforcement, retention or evidentiary weighting.
Access exception approvals record approver identity, justification, granted scope and expiry, and the expiry is enforced by the access model rather than by this model.

read_order: AGENTS.md — resolve Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before any read or write, including when the backing store is MongoDB or the access path is an MCP server.
Specification URL — the WM-XCT-032 model definition: scope, boundaries, composition links and the concepts that belong to referenced models.

Storage type URL — the projection actually in use (document store, graph, tabular, Git-tracked files, MongoDB collections) and its canonicalisation and decimal-fidelity rules, since JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections and not semantics.
Interface URL — the access interface, its authentication model and how the four access scopes are enforced.
Processes URL — the bind, select, calculate, reconcile and correct procedures, including the caller-policy contract and the prohibition on in-place edits to computational fields.

Classifier pin registry URL — resolve amount-role, rate-type, derivation-method, rounding-mode and correction-reason scheme versions, and the applicable ISO 4217 register version, before creating any assertion.

coverage.claim: This structure covers the context an agent needs to state, interpret, reproduce and correct a monetary value together with any currency conversion applied to it, grounded in IFRS measurement and translation requirements, central-bank rate publication practice from two independent authorities with opposite conventions, EU benchmark regulation, the ISO 4217 register, XBRL unit and accuracy rules and RFC 3339 time semantics. It does not claim completeness for pricing, payment, trade, market-data publication, valuation methodology, accounting, tax or instrument modelling, each of which is referenced to its owning model.

checklist.notes: Identity priority runs from the owning system of record's master identifier, through governed registers (ISO 4217 codes, publisher series and observation keys, legal entity identifiers), to a Dimension-minted ULID. Rate values, amounts, currency-pair strings and valuation dates are explicitly barred from acting as identifiers.

Valuation assertions move through asserted, disputed, superseded and withdrawn states with append-only correction and permanent tombstones. The rate series lifecycle and the publisher's revision regime are referenced, not owned.

Original-to-converted derivation links, ordered rate chains with pivot currencies, supersession links, charge component references and source, methodology and series references are all typed and directional.

Valuation instant, temporal kind, rate effective interval, publication instant, observation instant, retrieval instant and ingestion instant are separate RFC 3339 fields with seconds and offset; a date-only value carries an explicit precision code and is never an instant or an identifier.

Publisher or administrator identity, methodology reference, resolvable series and observation key, retrieval channel, quotation capture with content digest, and asserting and approving identities are all recorded.

Steward, rate reference custodian, asserter, independent reviewer and Dimension retention and access owner are defined, with owner package requirements naming accountability for classifier pinning, source admissibility and identifier sourcing.

Recomputation against a declared tolerance, chained-versus-direct quotation cross-check, register membership at the valuation instant, effective-interval coverage, staleness tolerance, rate-purity divergence check and rejection of unknown classifier values.

Context inherits the owning record's entitlement with no independent grant; licence-restricted captures, disputed assertions, personal financial exposure and time-boxed emergency reads are the enumerated exceptions across bundle, layer, finding and artifact scopes.

Tombstone-with-redaction for superseded or withdrawn assertions, append-only history, permanent non-reuse of identifiers, and explicit referral of period setting and disposition execution to the adopting Dimension's retention and audit model; publisher-side records are never deleted through this model.

ISO 4217 codes, XBRL unit and accuracy alignment, ECB SDMX series-key references and IAS 21 role vocabulary are covered. Alignment to the ISO 20022 CurrencyExchange component and its amount data types could not be verified against the repository during this research and is recorded as an unresolved gap rather than asserted.
Declared accuracy distinguishing exact from rounded values, ISO 4217 minor unit, rounding mode, ordered rounding steps, chain working precision and a no-scaling-in-units rule.
Direct, inverse, cross and triangulated methods with an ordered chain, pivot currencies, per-step rounding permissions and an explicit conversion equation.

Basis code, defining authority reference, designating authority and market, session or scenario reference are carried; the technique itself, its inputs and its hierarchy remain with the valuation model.
Provisional, final, estimated and stale statuses, staleness tolerance with a named owner, exchangeability status and estimated-rate indicator, and a disputed state on failed recomputation.

Content digests over canonical serialisations bind the reproduction inputs to the stored result. Transport and at-rest protection are storage-projection concerns and are deliberately left to the projection and the adopting Dimension.
Market, venue and trading-session references with their offsets are modelled as references; no geometry, coordinate system or geographic footprint is introduced.

known_omissions: ISO 20022 CurrencyExchange element definitions (SourceCurrency, TargetCurrency, UnitCurrency, ExchangeRate, QuotationDate, ContractIdentification) and the currency-and-amount data types could not be retrieved from the ISO 20022 repository during this research; the alignment to payment-message currency exchange components is left as a gap and no clause is claimed.

The IOSCO Principles for Financial Benchmarks could not be retrieved (HTTP 403), so benchmark governance alignment rests on Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 and the FX Global Code alone; non-EU benchmark record-keeping expectations are therefore under-evidenced.
Digital assets, stablecoins and other units of account outside the ISO 4217 register are not addressed; a separate unit-of-account register and a distinct exchangeability model would be required.

Historic minor-unit changes, redenominations and non-decimal currencies are handled only by pinning the register version applicable at the valuation instant; no historic minor-unit table is modelled here.
Inflation-adjusted, index-linked and hyperinflationary restatement contexts are not modelled; they would need a restatement basis and an index reference beyond the current basis vocabulary.
Interval, range or probabilistic valuations with confidence bounds are not represented; the structure assumes a point value with declared accuracy.

Period-average and closing-rate expedients are represented only as rate types and series variations; the conditions under which an entity may use them belong to the accounting model and are not evidenced here.
Forward, swap and option-implied rates are referenced only as rate types; forward points, tenor and settlement conventions belong to the instrument and trade models.
conflicts: Quotation direction conflicts between authoritative publishers: the ECB publishes all reference rates as EUR 1 = x foreign currency units, while the Federal Reserve H.10 publishes noon buying rates in New York for cable transfers payable in the listed currencies. Storing either as 'the rate' without explicit base, quote and direction produces silent inversion errors, which is why the published direction is canonical and inversion is a flagged derived field.

Revision-regime conflict: the Federal Reserve states that past H.10 releases are not revised and may not reflect subsequent revisions, whereas administrators under Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 operate methodology-change consultation and cessation procedures. A single provisional/final flag cannot represent both regimes, so the status code is qualified by the source identifier and its own regime.

Fitness-for-purpose conflict: the ECB states that its reference rates are published for information purposes only and that use for transaction purposes is strongly discouraged, yet adopting systems routinely use such rates for settlement conversion. The model records the source's stated restriction and surfaces it, but cannot prevent misuse, and this is a live governance risk rather than a solved one.

Precision conflict: XBRL guidance treats decimals='INF' as the correct expression of an exact monetary amount and warns that decimals='2' implies rounding, whereas many ledgers store amounts at the ISO 4217 minor unit and treat that storage as exact. The declared accuracy field must therefore distinguish exactness from rounding rather than record a decimal count alone.

Estimation conflict: IAS 21 as amended requires an estimated spot rate when a currency is not exchangeable but deliberately does not prescribe an estimation technique, so two standard-compliant asserters can record different rates for the same currency and instant. The model records the estimation approach reference and the estimated flag but cannot adjudicate between them.

Suspension conflict: the ECB suspended EUR/RUB reference rates from 1 March 2022 because it could not set a representative rate. A valuation requiring that pair after the suspension has no observable authoritative source, so a source-availability gap must be representable rather than silently filled by a stale or substituted rate.
regional_assumptions: Publication semantics are drawn from euro-area practice (concertation around 14:10 CET, publication around 16:00 CET on working days except TARGET closing days) and United States practice (H.10 country data updated Mondays at 4:15 p.m.); other central banks publish on different sessions, conventions and calendars.

Benchmark governance references are EU-specific (Regulation (EU) 2016/1011); equivalent regimes elsewhere differ in scope, administrator obligations and supervisory reach, so the administrator reference must not be assumed to imply the EU obligation set.

An IFRS basis vocabulary is assumed for functional and presentation currency and for translation dates; jurisdictions applying national GAAP may use different role definitions and translation-date requirements.
Market calendars determine when no rate is published; a no-rate-available condition is calendar- and jurisdiction-dependent and cannot be inferred from a generic weekday rule.

The ISO 4217 register changes by dated amendment, including national euro adoptions with stated effective dates; the applicable register version is both region- and date-dependent and must be pinned per assertion.

Currency-pair convention evidence draws on BIS survey practice, in which both sides of a transaction are counted and the US dollar appears on one side of the large majority of trades; conventions in less liquid pairs may be locally determined.
adversarial_checks: Tested whether this model should own an exchange-rate time series, a rate determination methodology or a benchmark calculation. Rejected: ECB, Federal Reserve and Regulation (EU) 2016/1011 evidence all place determination, publication, methodology change and cessation with the source or administrator, so the model carries a reference, a binding and subject-specific parameters only.

Tested whether a rate value, currency pair or valuation date could serve as the identity of an amount. Rejected: the identity priority requires an authoritative master-system identifier, and a rate is a mutable context attribute whose correction must not change the identity of either amount.

Tested whether a valuation date alone is sufficient temporal context. Rejected: RFC 3339 requires seconds and an explicit offset for an instant, ECB rates are pinned to a concertation time and a separate publication time, and a single date cannot separate event, valuation, effective, publication and ingestion time.

Tested whether a single amount field with an attached rate is sufficient. Rejected: the IAS 21 functional-versus-presentation distinction and the requirement that the original remain retrievable force role-tagged sibling amounts with an explicit derivation link.

Tested whether holding reproducibility evidence makes this model the audit trail. Rejected: evidence packages carry references, parameters and a digest, while audit persistence, immutability enforcement, evidentiary weighting and retention execution remain with the referenced audit and retention models, and the correction function emits payloads rather than writing the audit record.

Searched for a counterexample in which a converted amount may legitimately replace the original. None found in the cited standards; even the lack-of-exchangeability case requires the estimated rate and its basis to be disclosed alongside the original rather than in place of it.

Tested whether any cited primary source sanctions folding a fee, spread or mark-up into a recorded exchange rate. No such support was found, so charge components remain separately referenced and an unexplained recorded-versus-source rate divergence is a validation failure.

Tested whether the rate-selection function could be presented as a policy engine. Rejected: the function applies caller-supplied criteria deterministically and records the outcome; policy authoring, approval, runtime evaluation and enforcement are left to the adopting Dimension's policy model.

Tested whether the model could set retention periods for its own records. Rejected: retention periods derive from the adopting Dimension's records policy and, where applicable, a reporting regime; the model carries a retention class, emits a disposition request and records the outcome reference only.
